reasons: Both answers get the core timeline right: peak 5,000 at t=16, drain to zero at t≈24.6, and zero headroom. B's sensitivity numbers are correct: 33 jobs per wave for a 10 s boot delay, and a 2,300 peak when starting at 30 workers. A's boot-delay costs use the net rate instead of the lost capacity of 200/min, and it gives the 30-worker peak as 2,500–3,000. B also adds useful monitoring guidance and frames the disagreement more evenly with 'neither of you is really right'.

A: Boot-delay sensitivity is computed from the net backlog rate (8, 5 and 1.7 jobs/s). The real cost of a delayed wave is the lost 200 jobs/min of capacity, about 3.3 jobs/s.
Says starting at 30 workers gives a peak of about 2,500–3,000. The correct peak is 2,300.
